coverage.main: Read all sixteen pages of arXiv 2002.03043v2 (11 June 2020): Sections 1-7, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-2, Figures 1-3, references and Appendices A-D (transformations, dataset sizes Table 3, 5-adversary sampling Table 4, full results Table 5). The corpus lists only the arXiv record.
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-D are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 1-2, 4-5 and Figures 2-3 evaluate semantics-preserving program-transformation attacks (random or gradient-based sketch filling) directly on the evaluated seq2seq/code2seq model, including adversarially trained models. No adversarial program crafted on one model is evaluated on another.

f1.evidence: Clean test F1 is reported beside adversarial F1 for every model, positive setup evidence, but no transfer evaluation exists.

f2.evidence: Every test point is attacked on the evaluated model; no transfer denominator exists.

f5.evidence: Budgets are numbers of program transformations k, a discrete non-Lp constraint; no transfer result exists.

f6.evidence: No transfer configuration exists, so this is neither a transfer recomputability success nor a failure.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed; the paper cites third-party model code (IBM pytorch-seq2seq, code2seq) and transformation tools; no transfer artifact applies.

bounds_exclusion.reason: Only direct attacks on the evaluated model are reported.

limitations: Retained in the frozen corpus with non-applicability reasons; the random adversary is black-box but not a transfer attack.
